page.title: Five Claude prompts we actually tested
page.sub: Everyone posts Claude prompts. We ran these five ourselves before sharing them, and each link below opens its own free guide with the prompt, our result and the steps.
page.prompt_how: Pick the one that fits what you need today. Each link opens its own guide with the full prompt to copy.
page.prompt_note: Four are prompts for any Claude chat. The fifth is a free skill for Claude Code.

results.name: Business idea: 19 of 100 fake customers bought
CV: 7 of 100 hiring managers said yes
Old stuff: six things priced at $655
YouTube skill: an 18-minute video in 88 seconds

page.tested_text: Every number in the reel is from our own run. A **$39 snack box** tested on 100 fake customers: **19 bought**, 81 passed. A sample CV tested on 100 hiring managers: **7 said yes**. Photos of six things we don't use: priced at **$655**. A strict tutor: we gave it **two wrong answers on purpose** and it caught both. A skill that watches YouTube: an **18-minute video back in 88 seconds**. **These are our results. Yours will be different**, because your idea, CV and stuff are different.
page.tip: **The tip:** start with the one that solves this week's problem. One prompt you actually use beats five you save.

followups.label: Not sure which one to use
followups.prompt: Here's what I'm working on this week: [describe it in two lines]. I have five prompts: one tests a business idea on 100 fake customers, one tests a CV on 100 hiring managers, one prices things I want to sell from photos, one is a strict tutor for any topic, and one learns from a YouTube video. Which one helps me most this week, and what exactly should I give it?
followups.note: Paste this into Claude and it will point you at the right one.

followups.label: Test any prompt before you trust it
followups.prompt: I found this prompt online: [paste it]. Before I rely on it, run it on a small example, tell me what it actually did, where it went wrong, and how you'd change the prompt to fix that.
followups.note: Almost nobody tests the prompts they share. This is how to test one in two minutes.

followups.label: Make a prompt your own
followups.prompt: Here is a prompt I use: [paste it]. Rewrite it for my situation: [describe your job or business in two lines]. Keep the steps, change the examples, and tell me what you changed.
followups.note: A prompt written for someone else rarely fits first time.

checklist.title: For the YouTube one, use Claude Code
checklist.detail: It is a skill, not a prompt, so it needs Claude Code (the Code tab in the Claude desktop app), on a paid Claude plan.

checklist.title: Run it on your own thing
checklist.detail: Your idea, your CV, your stuff. Our numbers are ours; yours will be different.

safety: **These are our results, yours will be different.**
**AI customers and AI hiring managers are kinder than real ones.** Treat the numbers as a first test, not a promise.
**The prices are estimates,** not offers. Check recent sold listings before you list anything.
**The tutor can still get things wrong.** Double-check anything that matters.
